abstract: In this paper†† This paper is published in the proceedings of EMNLP 2017. we show that reporting a single performance score is insufficient to compare non-deterministic approaches. We demonstrate for common sequence tagging tasks that the seed value for the random number generator can result in statistically significant (p<10−4p<10^{-4}) differences for state-of-the-art systems. For two recent systems for NER, we observe an absolute difference of one percentage point F1F\_{1}-score depending on the selected seed value, making these systems perceived either as state-of-the-art or mediocre. Instead of publishing and reporting single performance scores, we propose to compare score distributions based on multiple executions. Based on the evaluation of 50.000 LSTM-networks for five sequence tagging tasks, we present network architectures that produce both superior performance as well as are more stable with respect to the remaining hyperparameters. The full experimental results are published in [Reimers and Gurevych (2017)](#bib.bib30 "").11 1 [https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06799](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06799 "") The implementation of our network is publicly available.22 2 [https://github.com/UKPLab/emnlp2017-bilstm-cnn-crf](https://github.com/UKPLab/emnlp2017-bilstm-cnn-crf "")

bibliographic.title: Reporting Score Distributions Makes a Difference: Performance Study of LSTM-networks for Sequence Tagging
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

content.problem: Comparing single performance scores for neural networks causes false conclusions because different random seeds make models converge to distinct local minima that generalize differently.
content.proposed_solution: The authors propose comparing score distributions across multiple runs with different random seeds and evaluating network design choices across thousands of configurations.

content.claim: Comparing score distributions prevents false conclusions caused by random seed variations and identifies LSTM configurations that improve performance and stability across sequence tagging tasks.
author_stated_limitations: The authors only evaluated pre-trained word embeddings provided by other researchers rather than testing the underlying embedding-generation algorithms.

evidence.problem_quote: In conclusion, if the fact of different local minima is not taken care of and single performance scores are compared, there is a high chance of drawing false conclusions and either rejecting promising approaches or selecting weaker approaches due to a more or less favorable sequence of random numbers.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: Instead of publishing and reporting single performance scores, we propose to compare score distributions based on multiple executions. Based on the evaluation of 50.000 LSTM-networks for five sequence tagging tasks, we present network architectures that produce both superior performance as well as are more stable with respect to the remaining hyperparameters.
evidence.claim_quote: In this paper, we demonstrated that the sequence of random numbers has a statistically significant impact on the test performance and that wrong conclusions can be made if performance scores based on single runs are compared.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: Note we only evaluated the pre-trained embeddings provided by different authors, but not the underlying algorithms to generate these embeddings.
